title: Decision models (Connections -> Decision model)
change: New optional global Decision model, picked under Connections -> Connection defaults -> Decision model (default None). It answers a statement about the recent chat with a probability 0-1 compared to a threshold (yes/no), or picks one option from a short list. Three ways to get one: a local model you already run (Primary or Utility local model), a hosted Decision connection (TypeSafe/Jev, OpenRouter, user-run System One; plus an OpenAI-compatible chat model source), or the installable Open-Jev decision sidecar. Used by custom-agent activation questions, {{#if decision:...}} prompt statements, lorebook Decision fields, Smart response order (and optionally Advanced Memory). Without one, every feature falls back (statements read as no). New guide docs/connections/decision-models.md covers which to pick, incl. Termux (hosted connection is the practical phone choice).

title: Custom agent Activation questions
change: Custom agents can have an optional Activation question answered by the Decision model to skip irrelevant turns. Question and keyword controls share one activation card; Activation Keywords and cadence (Trigger Cadence) still apply; a failed or missing decision leaves the agent eligible to run. Per docs: question up to 500 chars, macros allowed, uses the agent's Scan Depth; per-agent threshold 'Run when probability is at least'; 'Bypass the question after this many messages' safety valve; write it as a statement of fact ('The latest message moves the scene to a new place'), not a question. Decision connections support TypeSafe, OpenRouter, and user-run System One endpoints incl. linked OpenRouter credentials.

title: Decision sidecar (installable decision model)
change: Marinara can download and run a purpose-built decision model (Open-Jev) as its own local process, independent of any local chat model.
